name: tree_oak
prompt: Use your image generation tool. The attached image is a reference: the old oak of the grove, 32x32 pixels, from our top-down pixel-art game, shown enlarged on magenta. Generate a NEW image of the same the old oak of the grove - same design, same colors, same top-down three-quarter view - redrawn as pixel art 128 pixels wide and 128 pixels tall, far more pixels than the reference, with A broad rounded crown of leaf clusters in three greens lit from the upper left, a thick trunk with bark lines and a hollow, roots gripping the ground, moss on one side; the tree fills the 128x128 frame. Draw at full pixel density and fill the frame; no part thinner than 3 art pixels.. Every pixel stays a crisp square of one flat color, no anti-aliasing, each one about 1/128 of the drawing's width: draw no smaller pixels than that. Thick dark navy outline one pixel wide. Painterly pixel art: every surface shifts hue as it turns from light to shadow (warm lights, cool darks), with ambient light and colour bounced from neighbouring parts, visible material texture (wood grain, stone pores, cloth weave) drawn in pixels, and an outline whose colour follows the surface it borders rather than one flat dark line. Rich colour, as many shades as the object needs. Solid flat pure magenta #FF00FF background around it, no text, no shadow, no extra objects.  The 128x128 drawing fills most of the image. Do not process the image with code afterwards; just generate it and save it as tree_oak.png in the current directory.
warnings: drawn on 166x175, between one and two times the grid: small shapes break up when voted to 128x128; draw it again with fewer, bigger details
